 Judgment

The plaintiff has filed this suit seeking for an order restraining the defendant No.1 and his men from interfering with her lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule 'A' property and from restraining the defendant No.1 from illegally and unlawfully opening a mutton and chicken stall at schedule 'B' property.

The plaintiff has also sought for direction to the defendant No.2 BBMP not to issue licence for opening the illegal and unlawful mutton and chicken stall at the 'B' schedule property and to direct the defendant No.2 to take legal action against the defendant No.1 for attempting to open the unlawful mutton and chicken stall at the residential and temple area located at the 'B' schedule property and for grant of such other relief's.

The plaint averments in brief is that the husband of the plaintiff Sri. Lakshmaiah Reddy was the absolute owner of 1/3rd portion of the vacant land bearing No.28/1 (156) Chalta No.33 P.T. Street 1230 of Domaluru measuring East to West 59 feet and North South 20 feet bounded on the East by property of Venkataswamy and 10 feet road, West by Drain, North by the share of Gopal Reddy and Gajendra Reddy and South by vacant land having acquired the same by a Chitta of properties and disclaimer dated 11.11.1981 which was executed by her father-in-law Sri.Pillaiah in favour of her husband.

The husband of the plaintiff being the absolute owner of his share had constructed a dwelling house for his personal purpose and had also constructed houses for rent and has let out the houses on rents to various tenants.

After the death of her husband, the khata OS No.26574/2019 was changed in the name of the plaintiff and her name has been entered into the records of the BBMP and she is the absolute owner of the suit 'A' schedule property.

Smt.Leelavathi vs Sri.M.Shahjahan on 7 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174291301/
2

The defendant No.1 is the adjacent owner of the property bearing No.153/16, 14th Cross, Domaluru village, Bengaluru comprising of 3 shops on the ground floor and the residential houses on the 1st,
2nd and 3rd floor and he has been interfering with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of her property by attempting to open a mutton and chicken stall next to the plaintiff's property only in order to harass her, to knock away the property of the plaintiff.
Due to the foul smell and dirt and waste parts of animals that are littered, it has become difficult for the plaintiff and her tenants to lead a peaceful life.
The plaintiff along with her neighbors and other OS No.26574/2019 residence had lodged a complaint before the defendant No.2 authority on 18.09.2019.

On receiving the complaint the authority of the defendant No.2 had visited the place and since the place is a residential area with many temples situated, the defendant No.2 has directed the defendant No.1 to stop his illegal activities.
Subsequently the defendant No.1 kept quite for some period, but later again started with his illegal interference.
The defendant No.1 is an influential person and is continuing the illegal activities only in order to cause disturbance, mental harassment and illegal interference of the plaintiff's property.

In the month of November 2019 the defendant No.1 continued to renovate the vacant shop on the ground floor which is referred to as suit 'B' schedule property with an intention of opening the mutton and chicken stall.

The plaintiff OS No.26574/2019 approached the defendant No.2 authority once again and lodged an oral complaint but the defendant No.2 authority did not respond to the complaint, on which the plaintiff approached the Halasuru police on 16.11.2019 but the police refused to indulge the matter as it is civil in nature.
Hence, the plaintiff was constrained to file this suit and prays for decreeing the suit.
3. In response to the summons issued, the defendant Nos.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their counsels, but the defendant No.1 did not file the written statement.
The defendant No.2 authority filed the written statement denying the plaint averments.

4. The defendant No.2 in its written statement has contended that if the defendant No.1 were to do any business without the licence or sanction from the OS No.26574/2019 defendant No.2 they will take immediate steps against the defendant No.1.
Hence on these grounds the defendant No.2 as prayed for dismissing the suit.
5. In support of the plaintiff's case, the plaintiff got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 23 documents as Exs.P.1 to Ex.P.23.
The defendants have not led oral or documentary evidence.
6. Heard arguments 7.
Perused the materials on record.

8. The following issues have been framed in the case:-
1) Whether the plaintiff proves that she was in lawful possession of the suit schedule property as on the date of the suit?
2) Whether the plaintiff proves the alleged cause of action?

Smt.Leelavathi vs Sri.M.Shahjahan on 7 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174291301/
3 OS No.26574/2019 3) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to the relief of permanent injunction as sought for?
4) What order or decree?

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
 ISSUE No.1 :- In the affirmative  ISSUE No.2 :- In the affirmative  ISSUE No.3 :- In the affirmative  ISSUE No.4 :- As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 10. Issue Nos.1 to 3:-
The plaintiff has sought for a direction to the defendant No.2 authority not to issue license to open the stall and also to take legal action against the defendant No.1.
This relief claimed by the plaintiff is in the nature of Writ of mandamus against an authority which cannot be given by a Civil Court.

The only remedy for the plaintiff to seek direction against a OS No.26574/2019 Corporation or Government authority is only by way of approaching the competent authority seeking necessary direction to such authority.
Hence, the relief claimed by the plaintiff in respect of defendant No.2 is not maintainable in this suit.

11. The only point for consideration is to see whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief of permanent injunction against the defendant No.1 in respect of his opening the mutton and chicken stall near the suit schedule 'A' property and interfering with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule 'A' property.

12. The plaintiff in this suit has taken up the contention that the defendant No.1 has illegally and unlawfully opened the mutton and chicken stall next to the OS No.26574/2019 plaintiff's property in order to harass her and that she has lodged a complaint, along with the other residents before the defendant No.2 authority, on which the defendant No.2 authority have visited the place.
The defendant No.2 has directed the defendant No.1 to stop his illegal business.

Though the defendant No.1 has initially agreed for the same, subsequently he has started illegally interfering with the plaintiff's schedule property with an intention to cause mental harassment to the plaintiff and her tenants.
The photographs produced by the plaintiff, at this stage, goes to show that the business run by the defendant No.1 is situated within the residential area.
The residential area is having temples and educational institutions and places of warship.

The defendant No.1 though has appeared before the Court through his counsel he has not filed his written statement nor produced any documents to show that he has obtained necessary licence Smt.Leelavathi vs Sri.M.Shahjahan on 7 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174291301/
4 from the BBMP to open the shop in the premises next to the property of the plaintiff, that too, in the residential area.
By remaining absent and not producing any documents, nor cross examining the plaintiff, the defendant No.1 has unequivocally admitted to the claim of the plaintiff.

The documents produced by the plaintiff goes to show that since year 2019 onwards she has filed several complaints against the defendant no.1 in respect of the interference caused by the defendant No.1.

The plaintiff has also produced the notices issued by the BBMP/defendant no.2 to the defendant No.1, OS No.26574/2019 stating that the licence has not been issued to the defendant No.1 to run his business.

14. The meat shops are regulated as per the directions of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act,
1976 and the provisions of the Prevention of the Food Adulteration Act are also applicable for food items.
According to the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, the illegal and unauthorized slaughter and sacrifices of animals in the public places is strictly prohibited.

It also states that any meat licenced shop should be handed over to the solid waste management compactors or autorickshaws authorized by the BBMP as disposal of such waste in public places is prohibited.

The Foods, Safety and Standards Authority of India has observed that roadside meat shops lacks basic infrastructure and hence, it has directed all OS No.26574/2019 Food Safety Commissioners and Secretaries of Urban Local bodies in the year 2014 to close the shops if they failed to meet the hygiene standards within a defined time.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 15. Sec.353 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, says that "no place within the limit of the City shall be used for any purpose mentioned in Schedule-X, without a licence obtained from the Commissioner, except in accordance with the conditions specified therein.

The Commissioner shall,
so required by the Corporation publish a notification in the Official Gazette and in two or more local newspaper that within a distance of five Kms. of the limits of the City shall not be used for any other purposes mentioned in the Schedule-X, without a licence obtained from the Commissioner and except in accordance with the conditions specified therein.

Provided OS No.26574/2019 that no such notification shall take effect unless sanction of the Government has been obtained thereof until the expiry of 30 days of the date of publication in the Official Gazette".

The Act also provides that "the Commissioner may at any time cancel or suspend any licence granted if he is of the opinion that the premises covered thereby are not kept in conformity with the conditions of such licence or with the permission of any bye-law made in this behalf, whether the licence is prosecuted under the Act or not" .

16. Sec.370 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act provides that "no person shall without the permission of the Commissioner or if the fees have been farmed out, of the farmer, sell or expose for sale of any animal or article, within any public market".
OS No.26574/2019 17.

The Ex.P.14 and 15 produced by the plaintiff also goes to show that the BBMP/defendant No.2 has refused to grant licence to the defendant No.1 to run the shop in the premises, considering that the premises is a place where there are temples and places of water drainage and accordingly the licence has not been issued.

Smt.Leelavathi vs Sri.M.Shahjahan on 7 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174291301/
5 18.

Hence, considering the documents produced by the plaintiff and the action taken by the BBMP/defendant No.2 in respect to the complaint lodged by the plaintiff along with the residents as per Ex.P.1, against the defendant No.1, it can be seen that the defendant No.2/ BBMP has taken action against the defendant No.1 in respect of the shop.

The defendant No.1 by failing to appear before the Court and contest the suit has failed to prove that he is running the shop in the 'B'
schedule OS No.26574/2019 premises by obtaining necessary licence from the BBMP and the plaintiff has proved that she is entitled for the relief claimed against the defendant No.1 restraining him from illegally interfering with her lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule 'B'
property.

19. Issue No.4:- In view of the reasonings given above, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The suit filed by the plaintiff is hereby decreed in part, with cost.
The defendant No.1 is restrained by way of a decree of permanent injunction, from interfering with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule 'A' property.
The relief of directions sought for by the plaintiff against the defendant No.2 is hereby dismissed.
Draw the decree accordingly.

--

(Yermal Kalpana) XXVI
